newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods - Diffs hold stable amid July expiry.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods - Diffs hold stable amid July expiry.

text.p: Differentials on prompt refined procucts were little changed late Monday amid a moderate gain in expiring July NYMEX contracts on unleaded gasoline and heating oil, players said.
July heating oil expired at 53.70 cents a gallon, up 0.37 cent for the day, while July unleaded expired at 58.12 cents, 0.21 cent higher.
Traders noted that July heat expired 0.15 cent less than Monday's settlement price for August material, while July unleaded expired at the same price as Monday's settlement price for August unleaded.
"July and August came real close together, so you won't see differentials having to be adjusted too much tomorrow" to compensate for the July-to-August rollover, one East Coast player said.
Most NYH differentials held stable in thin trade, with spot gasoline unable to benefit from the approach of the long Fourth of July weekend.

NYH conventional unleaded "M2" grade gasoline was offered at 3.0 cents below July futures, unchanged from late Friday, with "A2" reformulated slightly weaker at a half cent under the screen, players said.
Distillate diffs also held fairly true to late last week, with heating oil offered at 0.25 cent below July futures. Sun Co earlier Monday had posted a price of 0.05 cent under the print.
Midcontinent markets were unchanged in quiet activity. "It seems like a lot of people are already on vacation," said a Group Three trader.

Prompt June unleaded gasoline differentials in Group Three were pegged 3.50/3.75 cents to July NYMEX and any month July was at 1.50/1.75 cents. Chicago prompt July -- June is finished -- was pegged 0.25/0.50 cents over the print.

Group Three prompt low sulfur diesel differentials were also unchanged at 1.00/1.25 over July NYMEX. Prompt July was on par but any month barrels were a half cent higher amid anticipated demand from agriculture.
Chicago prompt July low sulfur was 0.50/-0.25 cents below the print with any month on par.
Prompt regular conventional "M1" gasoline firmed Monday in modest trading activity, according to market watchers, with many players limiting their involvement ahead of the holiday Friday.
Regular conventional gasoline for prompt delivery that changed hands at 2.75 cents under the August futures early in the day were seen bid at 2.50 cents under by late afternoon, according to traders.

Conventional "M1" for delivery near the end of the first week of July traded at 2.50 cents under the August futures, while end-July barrels were going for 3.00 cents under the futures, according to market watchers.

Distillate differentials showed little movement Monday, though prompt heating oil traded at 2.40 cents under August futures, the upper end of the range seen Friday. -- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
